summary: Players bid for landing rights and route tiles, extend their reach with better planes, and periodically cash out routes to the ever-encroaching Pan Am company for cash or stock; the stock holding becomes a slow-burn secondary win path alongside route-building. It plays as a light-to-mid auction and network game with historic event cards sprinkled in, moving at a brisk pace for its production values.
praised: Attractive, thematic production (planes, routes, historical flavor)
Auction mechanism for routes creates real tension and give-and-take
Approachable rules for the theme, plays quickly for a route-building game
Stock/buyout mechanic gives an interesting alternate path to points
criticised: Feels like a mashup of better games (Chicago Express-style stock, Ticket to Ride-style routes) without fully gelling
Randomness from dice/events can undercut careful planning
Limited long-term strategic depth once you've played it a few times
Runaway leader potential once someone establishes strong routes

scoring.why: The winner is decided mainly by cash accumulated from selling routes to Pan Am and any stock payout, with route income as the supporting engine.
